newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Mar 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Sunday declared that the 30 percent service quota for the freedom fighters would now be kept for their sons and daughters.
Sixty-five state-run industrial units have been slated for privatisation in the current fiscal year ending June.
The repatriation of Bangladeshi tribal refugees living in the Indian state of Tripura will resume on March 28.
Bangladesh has renewed its commitment to extend all possible political, economic, technical and military training facilities to Bosnia Herzegovina
Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Secretary General Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan on Sunday accused the ruling Awami League for distorting the history of the country's liberation war.
A clash between the workers of the ruling Awami League and the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) in the southern Khulna town left at least 50 people injured.
Bangladesh has framed a textile policy with a target to set up 1,200 textile units by the year 2005.

The Miner, a local private firm, is interested to take lease of the Baghaichanda Coalmine in Madaripur area for mining of peat coal, Energy Minister Noor Uddin Khan told the parliament on Sunday. REUTER
